intro.title: Introduction
intro.body_md: You are an associate at Ellingboe & Ravndal LLP. Your client is Cloverdyke Dairy Cooperative, a farmer-owned dairy co-op near Danforth, in Voss County, Meridian. The co-op operates a shared station where member farms' milk is received and cooled in a large bulk tank before it ships to a creamery. Last fall the co-op bought a new bulk milk-cooling unit from Brandt Refrigeration Systems, LLC for $96,000. Within its first two months, the unit failed to hold temperature three times, spoiling three tank-loads of milk and forcing the co-op to pay for emergency repairs and a rented portable cooler. Brandt says the co-op's own electrical service and lapsed maintenance caused the failures, and it points to a limited-remedy warranty that disclaims consequential damages like spoiled milk. The co-op's general manager, Nils Aaberg, is coming in for an initial interview. The parties' agreement requires mediation and then binding arbitration, so this is not a courtroom trial — it is a sale-of-goods, breach-of-warranty dispute headed toward ADR. Your job in this exercise is to interview the client, develop the facts, analyze the warranty and remedies problem, and counsel the co-op on its options. {#b:bc58bc15}

history.title: Procedural and Factual History
history.body_md: The co-op and Brandt signed an equipment purchase agreement on September 10, 2025 for a bulk milk-cooling unit at $96,000, with a written limited warranty, an express performance specification, a buyer maintenance schedule, and a clause requiring mediation followed by binding arbitration. Brandt installed the unit on October 15, 2025. Whether the manufacturer's required 48-hour commissioning test was performed is disputed; the commissioning fields on the installation record are blank. The unit then failed to hold temperature three times: November 3, November 24, and over the weekend of December 12, 2025, spoiling three tank-loads of milk that the creamery rejected. Brandt's technician responded to each call, replacing a contactor, resetting controls, and cleaning fouled condenser coils, and noted both a possible power-supply irregularity and lapsed maintenance. The co-op sent a warranty-claim demand on January 20, 2026 seeking replacement plus roughly $28,000 in losses; Brandt denied consequential damages on February 5, 2026 and offered only to re-inspect and repair. The co-op retained an independent engineer, who inspected on February 27, 2026 and found a mix of an installation/configuration defect, marginal undersizing, and an electrical imbalance. The co-op retained Ellingboe & Ravndal LLP in March 2026. No arbitration has yet been filed; the matter is in the pre-arbitration demand-and-investigation phase as of June 30, 2026. {#b:03680ca4}
